text.p: These are the leading stories in the Namibian press on Friday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Environment and Tourism Minister Gert Hanekom ruled out the possibility of compensation for the Kxoe community being removed from community-controlled areas used as tourist camps in Western Caprivi.
- The Namibia Agricultural Union expressed unhappiness with a government decision to give higher livestock marketing incentives to communal farmers than to commercial farmers.
- People from Rehoboth are destroying a camelthorn forest near the town -- chopping down 2,000-year-old trees for firewood.
- Environment and Tourism Minister Gert Hanekom said his ministry wanted to cooperate with people from communal areas and the private sector in deciding in land questions.

- Prime Minister Hage Geingob said there had been unprecedented international interest in the issue of a possible third term for President Sam Nujoma and the ruling party's plans to change the constitution.

- One of the biggest building projects in Namibian history is on the cards with Windhoek Municipality and a Malaysian state corporation signing an agreement to build a N$400 million hotel and casino complex in the city centre.
